steps.description: We start with the smallest building-block: every concrete vault in the repository declares that it **implements** `IFeeVault`. The interface only exposes three read/write methods that any fee-holding vault must respect.
Line 10 returns the ERC-20 that the vault manages, line 16 reports the amount that has accumulated, and line 23 defines the single, restricted way to move tokens out.
`IAlchemistTokenVault` builds on `IFeeVault` for **ERC-20** fee revenue. Besides the common getters, it tracks who is allowed to withdraw, lets anyone deposit, and exposes admin hooks.
Same `token()` getter (line 15) and the additional `alchemist()` vault controller (line 21).
Line 28 exposes `authorizedWithdrawers(address)` and the public `deposit` (line 34) & `withdraw` (line 41) user flows.
`IAlchemistETHVault` adapts the same pattern but for native ETH / `WETH`. Notice the `WETH` helper, ETH deposit convenience and identical admin surface.
Getter for the wrapped `ETH` `token()` (line 14) and a dedicated `depositWETH` entrypoint (line 20).
The shared `withdraw` method (line 27) plus the admin `setAlchemist` (line 33).
Events mirror the `token vault` while naming the controller upgrade event `AlchemistV3Updated`.

Putting it together:
-  All vaults must expose `token()`, `totalDeposits()` and permissioned `withdraw()` via `IFeeVault`.
-  `IAlchemistTokenVault` adds **ERC-20** `deposit()` and fine-grained withdrawer control.
-  `IAlchemistETHVault` introduces dual ETH/WETH deposit paths and equivalent admin hooks.
Concrete contracts (`AlchemistTokenVault.sol`, `AlchemistETHVault.sol`) inherit these interfaces and rely on the common `AbstractFeeVault` base, enforcing the unified API while specialising the deposit logic.
